deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Prevents the resource from being deleted. It has direct security and availability impacts because deletion can lead to the redundant network connections breaking.

description.description: An optional description of this resource. Provide this property when you create the resource.
description.rationale: Basic text documenting the core function of the resource. It also being optional means it has no direct security impact and is purely for description.

interconnect_group.description:
The URL of an InterconnectGroup that groups these Attachments'
Interconnects. Customers do not need to set this unless directed by
Google Support.
interconnect_group.rationale: The specific group of physical network circuits being used. It has a direct security impact as if it is misconfigured then redundancy may not function correctly.

name.description:
Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is created. The name must be
1-63 characters long, and comply with RFC1035. Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters
long and match the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means the first
character must be a lowercase letter, and all following characters must be a dash,
lowercase letter, or digit, except the last character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: This is the label to be used when locating this resource. Renaming or altering it in any way changes nothing about how it functions. No direct security impacts.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Determines which Google Cloud project owns the resource. Incorrect project assignment can cause the wrong access rules to be applied to it.

attachments.description:
Attachments in the AttachmentGroup. Keys are arbitrary user-specified
strings. Users are encouraged, but not required, to use their preferred
format for resource links as keys.
Note that there are add-members and remove-members methods in gcloud.
The size of this map is limited by an "Attachments per group" quota.

attachments.attachment.description: URLs of Attachments in the given zone, to the given region, on Interconnects in the given facility and metro. Every Attachment in the AG has such an entry.
attachments.attachment.rationale: Specific individual connections added to the list. Has security impact in that if two connections on the same physical line are added then there is no real backup despite listing otherwise.

attachments.name.rationale: This is a label for an entry in the list to keep track. Has no security impact in that it does not point to anything or change any behavior.

intent.description:
The user's intent for this group. This is the only required field besides
the name that must be specified on group creation.

intent.availability_sla.description: Which SLA the user intends this group to support. Possible values: ["PRODUCTION_NON_CRITICAL", "PRODUCTION_CRITICAL", "NO_SLA", "AVAILABILITY_SLA_UNSPECIFIED"]
intent.availability_sla.rationale: The specific reliability level being claimed. Incorrect configurations can lead to false indications of backup protections or setup rejections due to mismatched claim.
